chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and I was present, so he said: 'When I shave for the first Ihram, what should I do regarding the final shaving, and how much time is between them?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When there are two Fridays between them, fifteen days, then shave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the required time interval between the first and final shaving during Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Basir from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifies the temporal requirement for the Ihram of Hajj al-Tamattu' by linking the shaving of hair to the passage of time rather than a fixed number of days. The criterion of 'two Fridays' (jum'atayn) serves as a practical lunar calendar marker, ensuring a minimum interval of fifteen days between the initial shaving after Tawaf and the final shaving before entering Mecca for Umrah. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on clear, observable signs for ritual obligations, distinguishing the Tamattu' Hajj structure from other forms.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullahasws and I was present, so he said, ‘When the first shaving is done for the Ihraam, what should be done regarding the next shaving, and how much (time) should be elapsing between the two?’ Heasws said: ‘When there would be two Fridays between the two, fifteen days, so shave (the unwanted hair)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“Abu Basir once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was present, ‘How much time is required between two applications (of hair removers)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Two Fridays, after fifteen days you can apply again.’”
